mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the structural organization of nervous tissue with that of epithelial tissue?

options.A: Nervous tissue consists of neurons and neuroglial cells arranged in layers, whereas epithelial tissue is composed of tightly packed cells forming continuous sheets.
options.B: Nervous tissue possesses a central lumen, while epithelial tissue does not.
options.C: Both tissues have abundant extracellular matrix that provides mechanical support.
options.D: Epithelial tissue conducts nerve impulses, whereas nervous tissue is primarily protective.

mcqs.answer: Nervous tissue consists of neurons and neuroglial cells arranged in layers, whereas epithelial tissue is composed of tightly packed cells forming continuous sheets.
mcqs.explanation: Nervous tissue is made up of neurons (excitable cells) and supporting neuroglial cells, organized in layers such as the cortex and gray/white matter. Epithelial tissue, in contrast, is a continuous sheet of closely packed cells with little extracellular matrix, serving protective, absorptive, or secretory roles. Options B, C, and D describe features that are not characteristic of the respective tissues.

mcqs.question: In the human body, which tissue type is most directly adapted for rapid transmission of electrical signals, and which structural feature primarily enables this function?

options.A: Nervous tissue – presence of myelinated axons

mcqs.answer: Nervous tissue – presence of myelinated axons
mcqs.explanation: Rapid electrical conduction is a hallmark of nervous tissue. Myelinated axons have a fatty sheath that insulates the nerve fiber and allows saltatory conduction, greatly increasing signal speed. Muscular tissue contracts, connective tissue provides support, and epithelial tissue forms barriers; none of these are primarily for fast electrical transmission. Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.question: Epithelial tissue is primarily characterized by which of the following features?

options.A: Cells are closely packed with minimal extracellular matrix forming continuous sheets.
options.B: Cells are scattered in a large amount of extracellular matrix.
options.C: It contains long, contractile fibers for movement.
options.D: It consists of neurons and supporting glial cells.

mcqs.answer: Cells are closely packed with minimal extracellular matrix forming continuous sheets.
mcqs.explanation: Epithelial tissue forms continuous layers of tightly joined cells with little extracellular material, allowing functions such as protection, absorption, and secretion. Options B describes connective tissue, C describes muscular tissue, and D describes nervous tissue.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes connective tissue?

options.A: It is composed of tightly packed cells with no extracellular material.
options.B: It consists of relatively few cells scattered in an abundant extracellular matrix that provides support and binding.
options.C: It contains long, multinucleated fibers that contract to produce movement.
options.D: It is made up of neurons that transmit electrical impulses.

mcqs.answer: It consists of relatively few cells scattered in an abundant extracellular matrix that provides support and binding.
mcqs.explanation: Connective tissue is defined by a sparse population of cells (fibroblasts, adipocytes, etc.) embedded in a large extracellular matrix of fibers (collagen, elastin) and ground substance, giving structural support. Option A describes epithelial tissue, C describes muscular tissue, and D describes nervous tissue.

mcqs.question: Muscular tissue differs from epithelial tissue in that muscular tissue:

options.A: Forms continuous sheets with extensive tight junctions.
options.B: Has a large extracellular matrix that stores calcium.
options.C: Contains contractile fibers that enable movement, whereas epithelial tissue primarily serves protective and absorptive functions.
options.D: Is composed of neurons and glial cells.

mcqs.answer: Contains contractile fibers that enable movement, whereas epithelial tissue primarily serves protective and absorptive functions.
mcqs.explanation: Muscular tissue is specialized for contraction due to the presence of actin and myosin filaments, allowing movement. Epithelial tissue, on the other hand, forms protective barriers and participates in absorption and secretion. Options A and B describe epithelial characteristics, while D describes nervous tissue.

mcqs.question: A person touches a hot stove and quickly withdraws the hand. Which tissue type is primarily responsible for detecting the heat and transmitting the signal to the brain?
mcqs.explanation: Thermoreceptors in the skin are specialized nerve endings, part of the nervous tissue, that detect temperature changes and generate nerve impulses. These impulses travel via sensory neurons to the spinal cord and brain, prompting a rapid withdrawal response. The other tissues do not have sensory or signal-conducting functions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a structure‑function relationship in connective tissue?

options.A: Simple squamous epithelium allowing rapid diffusion of gases.
options.B: Dense regular connective tissue in tendons, where parallel collagen fibers provide tensile strength along the direction of force.
options.C: Cardiac muscle with intercalated discs enabling synchronized contraction.
options.D: Myelinated nerve fibers increasing speed of impulse conduction.

mcqs.answer: Dense regular connective tissue in tendons, where parallel collagen fibers provide tensile strength along the direction of force.
mcqs.explanation: Tendons are composed of dense regular connective tissue; the collagen fibers are aligned parallel to the line of pull, giving the tendon high tensile strength precisely where it is needed. Option A relates to epithelial tissue, C to muscular tissue, and D to nervous tissue.

mcqs.question: A drug needs to be absorbed quickly into the bloodstream from the intestinal lining. Which type of epithelial tissue is most suitable for this function?

options.A: Simple columnar epithelium with microvilli (absorptive epithelium)

mcqs.answer: Simple columnar epithelium with microvilli (absorptive epithelium)
mcqs.explanation: The intestinal lining consists of simple columnar epithelium that possesses a brush border of microvilli, dramatically increasing surface area for absorption. Stratified squamous epithelium protects against abrasion, transitional epithelium is found in the urinary bladder, and pseudostratified columnar epithelium with cilia lines the respiratory tract, none of which are optimized for nutrient/drug absorption.
